A wireless communication device is configured to transmit predetermined information to a corresponding master device at predetermined intervals. This transmission is performed using a time division multiple access (TDMA) scheme, in which communication is divided into a plurality of time slots and each wireless device transmits information during an assigned transmission period.

During wireless communication, the wireless communication device also acquires transmission information that is not directly addressed to itself. This unrelated transmission information is obtained from another wireless slave device that is communicating within the same wireless system. The unrelated transmission information includes identification information for the other wireless slave device, allowing the receiving device to recognize which device transmitted the information.

Based on the identification information of the other wireless slave device, the time at which the unrelated transmission information was acquired, and transmission sequence information indicating the order or timing of transmissions within the TDMA scheme, the wireless communication device determines its own transmission time slot. In this way, the device can autonomously identify an appropriate timing for transmitting its predetermined information without causing interference with transmissions from other devices.

By enabling each wireless communication device to determine its transmission timing using information obtained from surrounding wireless slave devices, the technology supports efficient use of communication time slots. As a result, it provides high-speed and highly reliable wireless communication, particularly for systems that collect information from multiple wireless devices.

In this system, a plurality of slave devices communicate wirelessly with a master device by transmitting information in assigned time slots, so that transmissions from different devices do not overlap. Each slave device is capable not only of transmitting its own information to the master device, but also of receiving and monitoring transmissions made by other slave devices in the same communication network.

The wireless communication device acquires transmission information from the other slave devices, such as identification information that identifies each transmitting slave device and timing information indicating when each device transmits. The device also obtains transmission sequence information that defines the order in which the slave devices are expected to transmit. Using the acquired identification data, timing data, and transmission sequence information, the wireless communication device determines an appropriate transmission slot for its own communication with the master device.

By determining its transmission timing based on actual information obtained from surrounding slave devices, the device can efficiently join or continue communication within the TDMA sequence without causing interference or collision with other transmissions. This makes it possible to collect information wirelessly from multiple devices at high speed and with improved reliability. The technology is particularly useful in systems where many slave devices must transmit data to a master device in a coordinated manner, such as sensor networks, monitoring systems, industrial control systems, and other wireless data collection environments.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for a wireless communication device that uses TDMA, listens to transmissions from other slave devices, identifies their IDs and timing, determines its own transmission slot from sequence information, and transmits data reliably to a master device.
counterfactuals.output: A wireless communication device configured for operation in a time division multiple access (TDMA) wireless network includes a receiver, a transmitter, and control circuitry. The control circuitry monitors wireless transmissions from one or more other slave devices, detects identification information and timing information associated with the transmissions, and determines sequence information defining an order of slave-device transmissions within a communication cycle. Based on the detected identification information, timing information, and sequence information, the control circuitry identifies a transmission time slot allocated to the wireless communication device. The transmitter then transmits data to a master device during the identified transmission time slot. By deriving slot timing from observed transmissions of other slave devices, the wireless communication device maintains synchronization and reduces slot conflicts, thereby enabling reliable communication with the master device in the TDMA network.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a formal patent summary for an invention: a wireless communication device periodically sends predetermined information to a corresponding master device, obtains transmission info from nearby unrelated slave devices, determines a transmission slot based on device ID, acquisition timing, and transmission sequence data, and improves high-speed reliable information collection.
counterfactuals.output:
A wireless communication device is configured to perform efficient and reliable periodic transmission of predetermined information to a corresponding master device. The wireless communication device includes a communication unit configured to transmit the predetermined information to the master device and to receive transmission-related information from one or more nearby slave devices that are not associated with the master device. The transmission-related information may include, for example, device identification information, information acquisition timing, and transmission sequence information relating to communication operations of the nearby slave devices.

A control unit of the wireless communication device determines a transmission slot for transmitting the predetermined information based on at least a device ID of the wireless communication device, timing at which the transmission-related information is acquired from the nearby slave devices, and transmission sequence data. The determined transmission slot is selected so as to reduce interference or collision with transmissions by other slave devices, including unrelated nearby devices operating in the same or an adjacent wireless environment.

By autonomously determining an appropriate transmission slot using information obtained from surrounding devices, the wireless communication device enables high-speed collection of information by the master device while maintaining transmission reliability. The invention is particularly advantageous in wireless systems in which multiple slave devices periodically transmit sensor data, status information, control information, or other predetermined data to a master device, and where stable communication is required despite the presence of neighboring communication groups.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Convert the following invention concept into patent claim/abstract language: In a TDMA wireless network, each device can overhear other slaves’ messages to their own masters, extract identification information, combine it with reception time and transmission order information, choose its own slot, then send its stored data.
counterfactuals.output:
## Abstract

A method and apparatus for slot selection in a time division multiple access (TDMA) wireless network are provided. A wireless device operating as a slave node monitors transmissions from other slave nodes directed to their respective master nodes. The wireless device extracts identification information from the monitored transmissions and associates the identification information with reception timing information and transmission order information. Based on the extracted identification information, reception time, and relative transmission order, the wireless device determines an available or appropriate TDMA transmission slot for its own communication. The wireless device then transmits stored data in the selected slot, thereby enabling distributed slot selection and reducing contention without requiring centralized slot assignment.

## Example Independent Method Claim

1. A method performed by a wireless device in a time division multiple access (TDMA) wireless network, the method comprising:  
   monitoring, by the wireless device, wireless transmissions from a plurality of other slave devices, each of the wireless transmissions being directed to a corresponding master device;  
   extracting, from the monitored wireless transmissions, identification information associated with the plurality of other slave devices;  
   determining reception time information corresponding to respective ones of the monitored wireless transmissions;  
   determining transmission order information associated with the monitored wireless transmissions;  
   selecting, by the wireless device, a TDMA transmission slot for the wireless device based at least in part on the extracted identification information, the reception time information, and the transmission order information; and  
   transmitting, by the wireless device, stored data during the selected TDMA transmission slot.

## Example Independent Apparatus Claim

2. A wireless device for use in a time division multiple access (TDMA) wireless network, the wireless device comprising:  
   a receiver configured to monitor wireless transmissions from other slave devices to respective master devices;  
   a processor coupled to the receiver and configured to:  
   extract identification information from the monitored wireless transmissions;  
   associate the extracted identification information with reception time information and transmission order information for the monitored wireless transmissions;  
   determine a TDMA transmission slot for the wireless device based at least in part on the extracted identification information, the reception time information, and the transmission order information; and  
   a transmitter configured to transmit stored data of the wireless device during the determined TDMA transmission slot.

## Example Independent Non-Transitory Computer-Readable Medium Claim

3. A non-transitory computer-readable medium storing instructions that, when executed by one or more processors of a wireless device in a TDMA wireless network, cause the wireless device to:  
   overhear transmissions from a plurality of slave devices to corresponding master devices;  
   extract device identification information from the overheard transmissions;  
   store the device identification information in association with reception timing data and transmission sequence data;  
   select a TDMA slot for transmission by the wireless device using the stored device identification information, reception timing data, and transmission sequence data; and  
   cause stored data to be transmitted by the wireless device in the selected TDMA slot.

## Example Dependent Claims

4. The method of claim 1, wherein the identification information comprises at least one of a slave device identifier, a master device identifier, a network address, a temporary identifier, or a link identifier.

5. The method of claim 1, wherein selecting the TDMA transmission slot comprises identifying a slot not occupied by any of the monitored wireless transmissions.

6. The method of claim 1, wherein selecting the TDMA transmission slot comprises determining a relative position of the wireless device within a transmission sequence of slave devices.

7. The method of claim 1, wherein the reception time information comprises a timestamp generated when a monitored wireless transmission is received by the wireless device.

8. The method of claim 1, wherein the transmission order information indicates an order in which the monitored wireless transmissions are received within a TDMA frame.

9. The method of claim 1, further comprising storing a table associating device identifiers with corresponding reception times and transmission order positions.

10. The method of claim 9, wherein selecting the TDMA transmission slot comprises updating the table over a plurality of TDMA frames and selecting the TDMA transmission slot based on the updated table.

11. The method of claim 1, wherein the wireless device selects the TDMA transmission slot without receiving a centralized slot assignment from a master device.

12. The method of claim 1, wherein transmitting the stored data comprises transmitting sensor data, status data, control data, or buffered application data.

13. The wireless device of claim 2, wherein the processor is further configured to detect a collision or slot conflict and select a different TDMA transmission slot in a subsequent TDMA frame.

14. The wireless device of claim 2, wherein the receiver is configured to monitor transmissions during a listening interval before the wireless device transmits the stored data.

15. The non-transitory computer-readable medium of claim 3, wherein the instructions further cause the wireless device to rank candidate TDMA slots according to observed occupancy determined from the overheard transmissions.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Create a legalistic “Consequently, provided is…” style description of wireless communication technology enabling high-speed, highly reliable data collection, involving master/slave devices, predetermined transmission intervals, TDMA, acquisition of unrelated transmission information, and time-slot determination.
counterfactuals.output:
Consequently, provided is a wireless communication technology for enabling high-speed and highly reliable data collection in a communication system including a master device and a plurality of slave devices. The master device is configured to communicate with the slave devices by time division multiple access (TDMA) using predetermined transmission intervals, each transmission interval including a plurality of time slots allocated or allocatable to respective slave devices. Each slave device transmits data to the master device in accordance with a corresponding transmission timing defined by the predetermined transmission interval.

The master device further acquires transmission information relating to wireless transmissions other than, or unrelated to, the scheduled data transmissions from the slave devices, such transmission information including, for example, channel usage, interference conditions, signal reception status, timing information, or occupation of one or more time slots by another wireless system or communication source. Based on the acquired unrelated transmission information, the master device determines one or more time slots to be used for communication with the slave devices, and controls allocation of the determined time slots within the TDMA transmission interval.

By determining the time slots in view of the unrelated transmission information, the system suppresses collision, interference, and retransmission, thereby improving communication reliability while maintaining high-speed collection of data from the slave devices. Accordingly, stable and efficient wireless data collection is achieved even in an environment in which other wireless transmissions may be present.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
